children: SYDNEY--Brookfield Asset Management has agreed to acquire Reliance Worldwide in an all-cash deal that values the plumbing-supplies manufacturer at US$2.9 billion.

Australia-listed Reliance, which operates domestically and in countries such as the U.S., Canada and Mexico, on Wednesday said Brookfield firmed its US$3.38-a-share proposal after four weeks of exclusive due diligence.
Reliance said its directors unanimously recommended the offer to shareholders, who could opt to receive in U.S. dollars, or 4.75 Australian dollars a share.
The stock was up nearly 5% at A$4.54 in early trade Wednesday.
Brookfield viewed Reliance as a global, market-leading industrial company with value creation opportunities, said Anuj Ranjan, chief executive of Brookfield's private-equity group.
"Brookfield's global operating expertise in industrials and the U.S. housing ecosystem positions us well to support Reliance in its next phase of growth and over the long term," Ranjan said.

Brookfield first approached Reliance in April. At the time, the stock had fallen about 50% over 18 months amid uncertainty over U.S. tariff policy and the impact of higher interest rates on demand for new housing, a key driver of orders for plumbing supplies.
Brookfield raised its offer from A$4.15 to A$4.50 across three proposals before Reliance opened its books for eight weeks.
Brookfield subsequently raised its offer to A$4.75 a share, persuading Reliance to grant it four weeks of exclusive due diligence through mid September.

Last month, Reliance reported that annual sales fell 0.7% over the 12 months through June. It only narrowly avoided a bottom-line loss after an Australian manufacturing overhaul resulted in US$103.3 million of one-off items.
Reliance expects the transaction to be completed by the end of March.
